newsitem.title: USA: Draft restrictions lifted on Houston Ship Channel.
newsitem.headline: Draft restrictions lifted on Houston Ship Channel.

text.p: Draft restrictions were lifted but traffic was limited to one-way at a time on Sunday along a section of the Houston Ship Channel where six large tanks sank in a barge accident last week, officials said.
"There's no draft restrictions, but there's only one-way traffic past the accident site," U.S. Coast Guard spokesman Jose Gutierrez said.

Crews were still searching for the tanks loaded with zinc bromide that fell overboard last Thursday after the barge they were on was swept by the wake of a passing ship, slowing traffic between mile 52 and mile 56 on the channel, he said.
The accident forced the Coast Guard to ban deep-draft ships from that section of the channel, which is used by tankers and freighters to reach the Port of Houston and refinery row.
Most delayed ships had sailed by early Sunday evening. "There's very little backlog," a Ship Channel Pilots dispatcher said.

A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers sonar ship determined the channel was not blocked by the tanks. Three were located by late Friday, and the sonar ship was set to continue its search for the remaining tanks at daybreak on Monday, Gutierrez said.
The Houston Ship Channel is the commercial waterway linking the Port of Houston to the Gulf of Mexico.
